Water

Water
FormulaH2O
Molar mass18.015 g/mol
Density0.997 g/cm3

Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O. It is a transparent, tasteless, odorless,[1] and nearly colorless chemical substance, and it is the main constituent of Earth's hydrosphere and the fluids of all known living organisms.

Its boiling point is 100 °C at 1 atm; the speed of sound in water is about 1,480 m/s, and its dielectric constant is ~80 (εr). The Greek letter α is often used for thermal diffusivity, and μ for viscosity (about 0.89 mPa·s at 25 °C).

Etymology

[edit]

The word water comes from Old English wæter, from Proto-Germanic *watar.
